marketingRemarks.marketingRemark: The Lanner at Crest View features a classic two-story living experience. The ground floor boasts a welcoming front porch, leading into the seamless open-concept great room and modern kitchen with a corner walk-in pantry and functional center island. For added convenience, a powder room is tucked away on the main level. Upstairs, the owner's suite offers privacy with its en-suite bathroom featuring a dual-sink vanity and spacious walk-in closet. Three additional bedrooms can be found on the second level, two of which feature their own walk-in closets. A full laundry room and two-bay garage add the finishing touch to this home.

schoolReviews.review: Franklin Elementary School is an exceptional institution that excels in nurturing young minds and fostering a love for learning. The dedicated staff members go above and beyond to create a supportive and engaging environment for students. The school's commitment to academic excellence, coupled with a strong emphasis on character development, sets a remarkable standard for education. With a rich array of extracurricular activities and a focus on individualized attention, Franklin Elementary School truly stands out as a beacon of quality education and holistic growth for every child fortunate enough to be a part of its community.

I would never send my children to this school again. We MOVED out of the school district to get out of the environment. It’s run down (I know school finances are tight). Programs/performances ran by the school are rushed and not organized and there’s hardly any room in the cafeteria to be present for awards and programs (get there an hour early and be prepared to be ambushed by the parents coming in for the next students awards. I’ve never been to a school like this and we’ve been in four elementary schools (we move for work.)

I love this school, it's one of the only reasons I want to stay where I live, so both of my kids can go here. I love all the staff and I go to the Parent Teacher Club meetings and it showed me how much the staff really cares for not only the children but all the families, siblings, and parents, and grandparents. They very caring to the needs of all the children and they do a great job of keeping all the kids safe and well taken care of. I love this school. My daughter loves her class, they really keep the kids busy and learning. She has learned so much!

schoolReviews.review: This school is by far worst from what my friends tell me. How does a third grader struggle to learn when the teachers don't teach them the correct way. Using too much technology to make their life easier isn't helping the kids. They don't even know how to use a dictionary book. Their homework is always a struggle for them because they're not taught how to do the homework. It's like throwing things at kids and expect them to learn. The office staffs are so inattentive and rude. Parking lot is chaotic when picking up the kids. Some teachers gives you an attitude when you go pick up your kids. Everyone seems rushed to go home and I feel like the school is all about getting money instead of improving it. No wonder California ranks the bottom in education, no one cares anymore.

Worst school my child has ever attended.. My daughter is in a fourth/fifth grade combo class and has went from a child who loved school to hating it and getting in trouble all the time. Her teacher is moody and depending on her mood is the amount of homework the children will get... My daughter frequently comes home with 2 hr+ of homework. In my opinon is too much. The teachers here love to give detention for EVERYTHING!! My daughter got a detention for forgetting to put her name on a paper... seriously?! Oh and if your child needs to use the restroom... you guessed it.. DETENTION!! Upon asking the principal why this is standard she says that they are teaching them responsiblity.. that if the teachers cant use the restroom during class neither should the children and that they are prepping them for middle school but i'm pretty sure in middle school you don't get detention for bathroom breaks unless you make it a habit. And i'm pretty sure a teacher should be able to hold needing to use the restroom better than a 8 year old!! Teacher parent communication here is a joke i've asked (teachers and vice principal) serveral times to be kept upd on my childs progress and still nothing!

This is our second year at this school. My child is in fourth grade right now and is very frustrated. My child's perception is that the teacher seems to favor girls over boys. He seems to be in trouble all the time for not showing his work and getting detentions for the same reason. He is very discourage and his grades keep getting worse. He has gone from being an excellent student to hating school and not wanting to go.

We have had 2 very organized, structured teachers (3rd and 4th grades). They are nice, and experienced, but they seem to care only about test preparation instead of what the child is ready to learn. In other words, if your kid is a slow learner, too bad. They are still given the same work as the other students and made to feel stressed that the tests are coming up. Areas that might actually motivate a person to learn, such as art, science, history, and music are virtually ignored because the focus is almost entirely on reading, writing and math skills. There is only so much drill these kids can take. My child is hating school because he has trouble finishing the given amount of work in the same time as other students. As a result, he has recess detention almost daily. The school has the same policy if they don't get the homework done. He is discouraged. We work with him at home, but he still struggles. I wish the teachers at this school would help each student develop their own strengths instead of making everyone feel guilty for not fitting in to their desired statistics. When you go to a conference, the teachers do not ask you anything or listen. Too bad.

schoolReviews.review: My eldest child went through this school and my youngest is currently enrolled now. I immediately must warn you….BEWARE of the assistant principal! She will speak over you if you have a concern and make matters MUCH worse. She’s a nightmare. I definitely recommend skipping her and going straight to the head Principal for your concern. He definitely takes care of business and will treat you with respect. Unfortunately this school has A LOT of kid drama. Just in this past 2 weeks there have been 6-8 fights. It got so bad that our kids called us to pick them up cause they were scared. I pulled up to a long line out the door of upset parents waiting to sign their kid out after lunch. School never called to let us know what was going on. It’s just absurd. When it comes to teaching, some teachers can be helpful and some are obviously there to get a paycheck. They don’t care. Don’t believe me… go check out the schools math rating. Last time I checked the percentage of students achieving proficiency in math is 29% (which is lower than the California state average of 40%). At what point are we not going to start blaming the teachers for this insane percentage? My youngest kid’s math teacher will not accept ANY late HW even if sick. I have a ton of college classes under my belt (100 units plus) and I’ve never encountered a teacher like this one. During the student teacher meeting, she either looked at me with a blank stare or just repeatedly said no with a smirk when I asked her if there was anything my kid could do to make up for it. I could go on and on about it but I’ll just leave you with this reminder….. there is a reason this school has a 3/10 rating. Can not wait till my kid is done with this school. Good luck to all you other parents and just pray your child can get through this school without feeling mentally beaten down.

I find the staff rude and often passive aggressive with students. That excludes the teachers though, or at least some. I find my teachers very nice, helpful, and caring although there is that one or two teachers at this school that I can describe more negatively. I feel like the way they solve problems at this school is not OK. They don't even bother to alert parents either most of the time when there's a student issue. Their dress code is ridiculous as well. They can dress code you for wearing red then put you in all blue. The overall learning and friends experience comes down to the student though. If your child or student wants to learn they will. The teachers provide sufficient help and guidance to make sure you can pass the grade. It's just up to the student to pay attention and the amount of motivation they have. One thing though is there is a lot of student drama. It can be fights or student encounters and just people who don't like each other. But there are ways you can avoid that and if you have a problem you can just go up to the office and they handle it. They can also have absurd rules, for example once you leave the field during lunch you can't go back on campus which I've tried to imagine why they would do that but i can't, it makes no sense. If it wasn't for my friends all being at Hoover, I would definitely switch schools.

I was put in detention for no reason after being called names and being cussed at. Supposedly I used "Profanity" against the kids cussing and calling ME names. I highly recommend to listen to your kid if they say they are being bullied at school and try to do something about it.

I have found the entire staff of this school to be exceptional team players in a cohesive effort to educate and enrich the lives and education of students in their program. They show genuine regard and respect for each and every student and parent in the program; as well as staff and auxilliary staff members. It has been my experience that, this team of exceptional educators, administrators, and classified staff, put out 150% personal and professional effort in the course of each and every day.

I have horrible experience with this school. Beware. My son don't want to go to this school. And the 6th grader teacher always picky and put my son on detention all the time. I can tell you more about how horrible my experience in this Cruikshank Middle School.

schoolReviews.review: Franklin Elementary School is an exceptional institution that excels in nurturing young minds and fostering a love for learning. The dedicated staff members go above and beyond to create a supportive and engaging environment for students. The school's commitment to academic excellence, coupled with a strong emphasis on character development, sets a remarkable standard for education. With a rich array of extracurricular activities and a focus on individualized attention, Franklin Elementary School truly stands out as a beacon of quality education and holistic growth for every child fortunate enough to be a part of its community.

I would never send my children to this school again. We MOVED out of the school district to get out of the environment. It’s run down (I know school finances are tight). Programs/performances ran by the school are rushed and not organized and there’s hardly any room in the cafeteria to be present for awards and programs (get there an hour early and be prepared to be ambushed by the parents coming in for the next students awards. I’ve never been to a school like this and we’ve been in four elementary schools (we move for work.)

I love this school, it's one of the only reasons I want to stay where I live, so both of my kids can go here. I love all the staff and I go to the Parent Teacher Club meetings and it showed me how much the staff really cares for not only the children but all the families, siblings, and parents, and grandparents. They very caring to the needs of all the children and they do a great job of keeping all the kids safe and well taken care of. I love this school. My daughter loves her class, they really keep the kids busy and learning. She has learned so much!

The growth I saw in my child academically and emotionally outweighed any concerns I may have had when we first started with this school. 8th grade was specially great! Mr. Cooper, Mr. Bromfield, Mr. Hart, and Mr. Church pushed my child to excellence. She went from thinking she was a B student to an "A" student. The principal, Mr. Ferguson is very supportive and hands on with students.

Even though the school academics are great, there is way too much drugs alcohol and violence on this campus. I am hoping to get into Mcswain school for my 8th grade year. I dislike this school with a passion.

schoolReviews.review: This school is amazing. Definitely has some of the best teachers you can find. Mr. Abejuela has a pull-up bar in his classroom and challenges students not only mentally but physically. Mr. Dissalvo always presents both sides to any argument so we could form our own opinions and even let us debate in the middle of class often. Mr. Wendel wrote a song and sang it with his guitar for our class at the end of the year, it was hilarious! Mr. Graham was an amazing science teacher and made learning about moles and the periodic table interesting. Ms. Alvarez was the most passionate teacher who ensured that each and every student had the help they needed to pass her class. Finally, Mr. Rivero always had a smile on his face and being in his class, even during Saturday school, brought happiness.

Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Merced High School and graduated in 2011. I was able to experience a variety of great teachers and learned skills I wasn't aware some schools don't have as a standard. They prepare students for jobs with mock interviews, resumes, cover letters and we covered a course on how to get into stocks. There was cooking and a home living elective class as well as many others. The school was also available to special need students and even though their classes were separate, they encouraged us all to have healthy interactions with eachother. So we'd have rallies and special events together. Another good benefit to the student is that the school has an open campus policy that gave Juniors and Seniors privileges to leave the campus during lunch as an insentive and if your academics are poor then you'd get the privilege revoked. If you are doing poorly in school, we have great counselors who care about your academics as long as you show an interest in wanting to succeed. They are also attentive to last year students, so that they are all prepared to graduate or even move on to other career paths. I received all these benefits as a student before the new high school was built and there was about 30 student average per teacher, so I can only imagine how great of an education these students can get going to Merced High School now with the new gym being built and a much more breathable school environment.

This school is simple and a bit old compared to the nearby schools. It has some problems such as old rooms and such stuff but overall appearance wise this school is okay. I like how the original Merced High School is the best overall school wise in the county. This school could improve by having more school spirit and landscape. In the old days this school actually had flowers!

schoolReviews.review: As I search for a new school (moving out of state) I found it baffling with the lack of reviews for private & faith based schools which brought me here. SRC has exceeded my expectations and everyone I’ve encountered since my children first started here four years ago has been amazing, loving, and caring. I honestly feel like this school is another “home” for my children and we will truly miss everyone there. We have been extremely happy with the academics and biblical studies they teach and are constantly in awe with how much our children learn. Seeing the joy in their eyes when they share their new found knowledge can’t be beat and the confidence they have gained the last few years, thanks to the teachers and staff, is amazing as well. SRC is truly one of a kind and we have been so blessed to have been a part of the knight family. If you’re even considering sending your child here, don’t hesitate. 100% worth it all around and has set our standards higher than before as we attempt to find something even halfway comparable.

We have two children at SR and two more coming up in the next few years. The academics and spiritual aspects have exceeded our expectations. The athletic programs are phenomenal. The family atmosphere has impressed us immensely. I couldn't imagine my kids at any other high school!

Stone Ridge is an excellent school and offers an excellent academic program. The academic program includes AP courses in English, Math, Science, and Social Studies. The school environment is incredible as the kids feel safe and they feel like they are part of a family. Kids can't wait to go to school every day! Stone Ridge offers an athletic program, leadership, choir, band, and more. Their average SAT scores are higher than all schools in Merced County. Everyone should enroll their kid at Stone Ridge.

Stone Ridge has been a part of our family for the last 8 years. My children have thrived there. Is it a perfect school . . . , no, but it's as close as it gets. Stone Ridge helped prepare my older boys for college; my oldest now has his B.A. and is attending Law School; while my other son is a Freshman at Azusa Pacific University. I currently have my youngest two children (a junior and a freshman), at Stone Ridge. Stone Ridge offers a variety of sports, has an Associated Study Body, celebrates academics, is involved in community service, hosts the SR Follies, has a great choir & worship team, all within the service of our Lord Jesus Christ. I have seen the staff go above and beyond in support of the students. I recently heard one senior say, "It's a small school so you know everybody. The teachers take time with you to help you. I feel loved there." As a parent I feel much the same way. Parents are always welcome to come and talk with the teachers, make suggestions regarding the school, help where their giftedness is, and fellowship with other parents at events and through the Parent-Teacher-Fellowship (PTF). I wouldn't have my children at any other school.

Stone Ridge Christian High School has been a wonderfull place for my children. My oldest son is now at the Airforce Academy and my daughter is now at Liberty University. My younger son is a sophmore at SRCHS. The school has small class sizes and parents can be very involved in their student's education. Every child can participate in student government or sports, and lots of AP classes are available.

Stone Ridge is an excellent school. i was reading someone belows comments. Jusf tyi, their is an outstanding sceince program with great equipment. Don't know how old that post is, but a new science teacher was hired and equipment added two years ago to the sceince program. AP Chem and AP Pys. is offered here. 100% of kids go to college and SAT Scores are 200 pts higher than public schools. Need I say more? Awesome School. I have a Soph at Stone Ridge and adding a Freshman next year. He can't wait to go. What a great environment.

Wind Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wind Model, which forecasts how hurricanes and costs from resulting wind damages to structures will change over time due to climate change.

A property's Wind Factor indicates its likelihood to experience extreme winds over the next 30 years, from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Wind Factor scores are more likely to experience higher winds more frequently today and in the future.

entryPointFlyout.value:
Flood Factor® is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street Flood Model, a nationwide, probabilistic flood model that shows a location’s risk of flooding from rain, rivers, tides, and storm surge. It builds off of decades of peer-reviewed research and forecasts how flood risks will change over time due to changes in the environment. Flood Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of flood.

A property's Flood Factor is an indicator of its comprehensive flood risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Flood Factors are more likely to have flooded in the past, and are more likely to flood in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property’s projected likelihood and depth of flooding, it has minor flood risk.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Flood risk accumulates over time. Cumulative risk is calculated to the largest building or center of an empty lot. Raised or elevated buildings may not be as vulnerable as ground-level buildings or buildings with basements.

Fire Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of fire.

A property's Fire Factor indicates its cumulative wildfire risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Fire Factors are more likely to be in a wildfire in the future.

Heat Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. Heat Factor™ uses the First Street Extreme Heat Model to determine property-specific heat risk across the United States. The model is a spatial temperature model that determines a specific location’s exposure to extreme heat events based on the surface temperature, topography, land cover, and humidity in the surrounding area.

A property's Heat Factor indicates its risk of extreme heat exposure over the next thirty years, ranging from 1 (minimal risk) to 10 (extreme risk). Heat Factors are based on the current average daily high temperature and humidity of a property’s specific location during the hottest month of the year, and considers how it’s expected to grow over the next 30 years.

A property may have more or less hot days than the surrounding area depending on its individual exposure to heat.
